classification.difficultyReason: Translate each labelled boundary into counts of a and b, then recognise its equivalent expression among the supplied partially or fully factorised choices.

inlines.text: Match the shapes with the expressions that show their perimeters.

spec.description: Unshaded hexagon with upper and lower points, two vertical sides labelled a and four sloping sides labelled b. Every side has an external double-ended dimension arrow.
spec.mathematics: The perimeter is 2a+4b=2(a+2b). Coordinates preserve the source silhouette and carry no additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Shape label and side labels are permanent givens. The matching letter is answer-only.

spec.description: Unshaded house-shaped pentagon with two sloping roof sides labelled a, two vertical sides labelled b and a horizontal base labelled b. Every side has an external double-ended dimension arrow.
spec.mathematics: The perimeter is 2a+3b=2(a+b)+b. Coordinates preserve the source silhouette and carry no additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Shape label and side labels are permanent givens. The matching letter is answer-only.

spec.description: Unshaded ten-sided shape with central upper and lower points. Four horizontal sides and two outer vertical sides are labelled a. Four sloping sides are labelled b. Every side has an external double-ended dimension arrow.
spec.mathematics: The perimeter is 6a+4b=2(3a+2b). Coordinates preserve the source silhouette and carry no additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Shape label and side labels are permanent givens. The matching letter is answer-only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P_{\mathrm{i}}&=2a+4b\\P_{\mathrm{i}}&=2(a+2b)\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=2a+3b\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=2(a+b)+b\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=6a+4b\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=2(3a+2b)\end{align*}$$
The matches are i–C, ii–A and iii–B.
